short: Atta — the engine for the Den: resolve, route, render
is: Atta, the host-agnostic engine for the Den: it resolves the tree, enforces its structural rules, asks the host about each node through one object-safe trait Atta defines, and renders files. Types and content are opaque to it; the host answers per type with an exhaustive match in application, never a runtime registry. It lives in this workspace as a crate only until it is split into its own library.
conventions: Never depends on another workspace crate and never names a Zurfur type — host-agnostic by construction, so it can be split out unchanged.
Used by application only; the API never imports it.
Its role is fixed: resolve, enforce structure, route changes, render. How it does that grows only as real needs appear, never ahead of them.
Nothing reads a node except through Atta; a payload is served only after its hash verifies, and until that check exists no payload is served at all.
Fails closed: one uniform not-found, no stored level means Private, and a mount whose target is not directly under a top-level directory is refused.
